summary: Gives guidelines for implementors and users on running OSPF over frame relay networks. Frame relay links connect many routers without behaving like a simple broadcast network, so careful configuration is needed. It is informational and does not define a standard.

eli5.summary: Frame relay is like a phone party line where not everyone can hear everyone. These tips help routers still share their maps correctly.

questions: how to run ospf over frame relay
how to configure ospf over frame relay
ospf frame relay full mesh problem
subtitle: Design tips for using OSPF routing efficiently on frame relay networks.

tldr.problem: OSPF's standard NBMA model for frame relay networks requires routers to be fully connected (a mesh of circuits), which becomes expensive as the number of routers grows.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC recommends treating individual virtual circuits (VCs) as logical interfaces and configuring them as point-to-point links rather than as part of a single NBMA network. This allows partial connectivity and assigns different link metrics to different VCs.
tldr.outcome: Network designers can build more cost-effective frame relay networks with OSPF without protocol changes; these recommendations are just configuration guidelines.

today: RFC 1586 remains an informational guide for implementing OSPF over frame relay networks. It has not been obsoleted and continues to be relevant for sites that use or maintain frame relay links.

sections.title: The Frame Relay Problem
sections.content:
Frame Relay is a wide-area network technology that creates virtual circuits (VCs) between routers, each identified by a Data Link Connection Identifier (DLCI). Frame Relay is characterized as a Non-Broadcast Multiple Access (NBMA) network in OSPF: it can connect many routers, but has no built-in broadcast capability like a LAN.

When OSPF treats a frame relay interface as a single NBMA network, all attached routers must be fully interconnected; that is, every router must have a direct VC to every other router. The cost of this full-mesh connectivity grows quadratically with the number of routers. Since public frame relay services charge per VC, the expense becomes prohibitive as networks grow. Additionally, the standard NBMA model assigns a single link metric to the entire interface, preventing routers from favoring better-performing VCs over worse ones.
sections.eli5: Frame relay is like creating phone lines between routers. The old way meant every router needed a line to every other router, which gets really expensive and complicated.

sections.title: Logical Interfaces and VC Groups
sections.content:
The RFC proposes a solution that does not require any OSPF protocol changes: configure the frame relay interface as multiple logical networks, each consisting of one or more VCs. A logical network containing a single VC is treated as a point-to-point link; a logical network containing multiple VCs is treated as an NBMA network, but only those VCs need to be fully meshed.

This approach allows a single physical frame relay interface to belong to multiple IP subnets, with each subnet corresponding to one or more OSPF interfaces. A point-to-point logical interface can be either numbered (with an IP address) or unnumbered. Numbered logical interfaces are recommended as simpler to implement.
sections.eli5: Instead of one big network, treat each group of connected routers as a separate small network. Some groups might be just two routers talking to each other.

sections.title: Configuration in Practice
sections.content:
To implement this design, an OSPF router should support numbered logical interfaces over frame relay in four configuration steps. First, configure the physical interface with frame relay encapsulation, DLCI details and parameters such as the Link Management Interface (LMI) and address resolution protocol (Inverse ARP if available).

Second, configure the network layer by specifying multiple logical interfaces and their IP addresses and subnet masks, associating each logical interface with its VCs (by DLCI). Third, configure OSPF on each logical interface, specifying its OSPF area, link metric, timers and the neighbor list for the Designated Router. Single-VC interfaces are configured as point-to-point links; multi-VC interfaces are configured as NBMA subnets.

The OSPF MIB should track these configurations. While unnumbered logical point-to-point links are possible in theory (using the ifIndex instead of an IP address), the RFC notes that this approach complicates the management information base and recommends using numbered interfaces instead.
sections.eli5: Configure the hardware, then the network addresses, then tell OSPF which routers are neighbors. Each VC or group of VCs gets its own settings and address.

sections.title: Network Design with Logical Interfaces
sections.content:
With the ability to configure logical interfaces, network designers gain flexibility. The RFC recommends building networks from small NBMA clusters (since the NBMA model provides economy in OSPF processing overhead for small homogeneous networks) connected by long-haul point-to-point links. The choice of cluster size and link metrics depends on frame relay pricing, service guarantees, traffic patterns and the desire to minimize OSPF overhead.

For networks that must be more flat in structure, assigning different link metrics to different VC groups allows routers to prefer circuits with better performance characteristics. This contrasts sharply with the standard NBMA model, which assigns a single metric to all VCs on an interface, and allows much more efficient use of frame relay network resources.
sections.eli5: Group routers into small clusters where they talk to everyone in the cluster, then connect clusters with single links. You can make some links more expensive than others if they are slower.

sections.title: Benefits and Conclusion
sections.content: The RFC's recommendations enable OSPF to run cost-effectively over frame relay networks without requiring any protocol changes. The approach is backward-compatible with existing OSPF implementations and allows phased deployment of the new configuration style. It gives network operators two key advantages: the ability to build partial-mesh networks rather than expensive full-mesh topologies, and the ability to assign different link metrics to different virtual circuits, making routing decisions more reflective of the network's actual performance and cost characteristics.
sections.eli5: These tips let you use OSPF more efficiently over frame relay without changing OSPF itself. You save money and can fine-tune which routes are best.
